title: Detection of a Nirsevimab-Resistant RSV-B Variant (F:K68Q) in an Adult with Severe Infection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to report on the detection of a nirsevimab-resistant RSV-B variant (F:K68Q) in an adult with severe infection, addressing the need for understanding resistance mechanisms in immunocompromised patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective, multicenter observational cohort study was conducted on a 64-year-old man with aggressive mantle cell lymphoma under active treatment.
analysis.methods: Nasopharyngeal samples were collected and analyzed for RSV-B lineage B.D.E.1, with genetic analysis identifying a dominant F:K68Q substitution in the fusion protein.
analysis.main_results: Two nasopharyngeal samples collected 7 days apart were positive for RSV-B, with the F:K68Q substitution detected at high allele frequencies in both samples.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The persistence of a resistant RSV variant in a monoclonal antibody-naïve patient suggests that such variants may circulate independently of nirsevimab exposure, highlighting the importance of RSV vaccination in immunocompromised patients.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that RSV vaccination of immunocompromised patients may help limit the dissemination of resistant strains, contributing to public health strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its observational nature and the small sample size, but the genetic analysis provides strong evidence for the presence of the resistant variant.

analysis.summary_en: This study reports the detection of a nirsevimab-resistant RSV-B variant (F:K68Q) in a severely infected immunocompromised patient, highlighting the need for RSV vaccination in such patients to prevent the spread of resistant strains.

title: Clinical and economic impact of bivalent respiratory syncytial virus prefusion F (RSVpreF) vaccination in older adults: a cost-effectiveness analysis for Chile.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of lower respiratory tract disease in older adults in Chile.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Cost-effectiveness was assessed from healthcare and societal perspectives in 2025 Chilean Pesos (CLP) and US Dollars (US$), with costs and outcomes discounted at 3% annually.
analysis.methods: RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: A population-based Markov model projected RSV-related outcomes under no vaccination and RSVpreF vaccination over the cohort lifetime.
analysis.main_results: At a threshold of CLP15,977,348 (US$17,180) per QALY gained, the maximum cost-effective vaccine price was CLP100,480 (US$108) and CLP265,261 (US$285) from the healthcare and societal perspectives respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: RSVpreF vaccination was projected to prevent 14,956 hospitalizations, 50,419 emergency department visits, and 124,849 physician office visits; avert CLP76 billion (US$82 million) in direct medical costs and CLP305 billion (US$328 million) in indirect costs; and generate 7,079 quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs).
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: RSVpreF vaccination would reduce RSV burden and likely be cost-effective for older adults in Chile.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: This deterministic extraction is based on retrieved fulltext evidence. The source does not explicitly report enough limitations for an independent appraisal, so confidence is low.

analysis.summary_en: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of lower respiratory tract disease in older adults in Chile. Cost-effectiveness was assessed from healthcare and societal perspectives in 2025 Chilean Pesos (CLP) and US Dollars (US$), with costs and outcomes discounted at 3% annually. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: A population-based Markov model projected RSV-related outcomes under no vaccination and RSVpreF vaccination over the cohort lifetime. At a threshold of CLP15,977,348 (US$17,180) per QALY gained, the maximum cost-effective vaccine price was CLP100,480 (US$108) and CLP265,261 (US$285) from the healthcare and societal perspectives respectively. RSVpreF vaccination was projected to prevent 14,956 hospitalizations, 50,419 emergency department visits, and 124,849 physician office visits; avert CLP76 billion (US$82 million) in direct medical costs and CLP305 billion (US$328 million) in indirect costs; and generate 7,079 quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs). RSVpreF vaccination would reduce RSV burden and likely be cost-effective for older adults in Chile. This deterministic extraction is based on retrieved fulltext evidence. The source does not explicitly report enough limitations for an independent appraisal, so confidence is low.

title: Molecular epidemiology of respiratory syncytial virus infections in Arizona, USA during the 2023-24 and 2024-25 seasons.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to surveil the sequence landscape of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) genomes to increase awareness of potentially neutralizing mutations, given the increased availability of vaccines and therapeutic antibodies. This is important for maintaining the efficacy of these interventions and for public health surveillance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: During the 2023-24 and 2024-25 RSV seasons, unpaired nasopharyngeal swab specimens were collected from patients presenting to Arizona healthcare systems with symptoms of influenza-like illness.
analysis.methods: Genome sequences for RSV and co-infecting viruses were obtained using tiled amplicon-based enrichment or a commercial oligo hybrid-enrichment panel and next generation sequencing. Phylogenetic and genomic analyses were performed to classify RSV genomes and detect mutations in the antigenic sites of the F protein and conserved central domain of the G protein.
analysis.main_results: Phylogenetic analysis showed RSV-A strains belonged to the A.D.1, A.D.2, A.D.3 lineages, and RSV-B genomes belonged to the B.D.4.1, B.D.4.1.1, B.D.E.1, B.D.E.5, and B.D.E. Over the two-season surveillance period, 9 polymorphic sites were found in the antigenic sites of the F protein in RSV-A genomes and 18 in RSV-B genomes. Additionally, 7 polymorphic sites in RSV-A and 8 in RSV-B were identified in the conserved central domain of the G protein. Viral coinfections were observed in 3 (6.7%) and 27 (15.8%) cases in the 2023-24 and 2024-25 seasons, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the importance of continued genomic surveillance to monitor circulating RSV variants and detect potentially neutralizing mutations. This is crucial for maintaining the efficacy of vaccines and therapeutic agents.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Viral genomic surveillance plays an important role in maintaining the efficacy of vaccine and therapeutic agents. Continued monitoring of circulating variants is an important component of public health.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study design limitations include the lack of randomization and the potential for bias due to the observational nature of the study. The sample size was adequate for the study objectives, but the generalizability may be limited to the Arizona healthcare systems. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study surveilled RSV genomes during the 2023-24 and 2024-25 seasons in Arizona, identifying mutations in antigenic sites and conserved domains of the F and G proteins. These findings underscore the importance of genomic surveillance for maintaining vaccine and therapeutic efficacy.

analysis.summary_en: ABSTRACT Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes substantial morbidity in pediatric hematopoietic cell transplant (HCT) recipients; however, risk factors for severe disease remain incompletely characterized. Methods We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study across 16 U.S. Univariate logistic regression was used to screen candidate predictors, followed by the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) for variable selection, and multivariable logistic regression to identify independent predictors associated with clinical outcomes. Results Among 204 pediatric HCT recipients with RSV infection, 41.7% had RSV-related hospitalization, 21.2% required new or increased supplemental oxygen, and 4% required invasive mechanical ventilation within 28 days after the diagnosis. Conclusions Severe outcomes are common in pediatric HCT recipients with RSV infection. These findings support targeted risk stratification and may inform preventive and treatment strategies in this high-risk population. Younger age, markers of impaired immune recovery, history of chronic lung disease, and T-cell–depleting therapy are major determinants of adverse outcomes.

title: Awareness and acceptance of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccination among pregnant women in Poland: Results of an internet-based survey.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants, particularly among vulnerable groups such as preterm newborns and infants with underlying medical conditions. The approval of the RSVpreF vaccine for use during pregnancy offers a new strategy for reducing RSV-related morbidity in newborns.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study conducted an internet-based survey among 668 pregnant women or recently delivered mothers in Poland. An anonymous questionnaire consisting of 23 questions was distributed via social media platforms between July 25 and August 1, 2024.
analysis.methods: A Computer-Assisted Web Interview (CAWI) survey was used to collect data. The questionnaire included 23 questions assessing awareness, acceptance, and knowledge of RSV vaccination.
analysis.main_results: Respondents with medical backgrounds more frequently provided correct answers to questions regarding RSV than those without medical training. For example, when asked about methods of treating RSV infection, 109 medical professionals (74.15%) answered correctly, compared with 251 non-medical respondents (48.18%; p < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights that medical professionals have better knowledge about RSV and its management than non-medical individuals. This finding underscores the importance of targeted education and communication strategies to improve vaccine acceptance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health campaigns aimed at increasing awareness and acceptance of RSV vaccination among pregnant women. They also emphasize the role of healthcare professionals in educating patients about vaccine benefits.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on self-reported data from an internet-based survey, which may introduce bias. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the study and potential self-selection bias among participants.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated awareness and acceptance of RSV vaccination among pregnant women in Poland through an internet-based survey. It found that individuals with medical backgrounds demonstrated greater knowledge about RSV and its treatment compared to non-medical respondents. The results suggest that targeted educational initiatives and public health campaigns could enhance vaccine uptake. However, the study's reliance on self-reported data and potential biases limits the strength of its conclusions. The findings highlight the importance of healthcare professionals in promoting RSV vaccination as a public health measure.

title: Relevance of Seasonal Revaccination against Respiratory Syncytial Virus in Hematology Patients: First Insights in Stem Cell Transplant Recipients

analysis.research_question_and_background: Abstract Several vaccines against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) have been commercialized recently.
analysis.study_design_and_population: In immunocompromised patients, the duration of vaccinal humoral protection as well as the relevance of seasonal revaccination is still unknown.
analysis.methods: The supplied evidence does not clearly state the core experimental, analytical, or statistical methods.
analysis.main_results: Their immediate immunogenicity in various conditions of immunosuppression, including patients receiving allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), have been reported in 2025 by different teams, including ours.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: We also provide a first evaluation of vaccinal clinical effectiveness in HSCT patients.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: By analyzing the kinetics of humoral responses after a single dose of bivalent RSVpreF vaccine over 12 months in 71 HSCT recipients, we show that annual revaccination benefits mostly those primarily vaccinated within the early 18 months after HSCT.

analysis.summary_en: Abstract Several vaccines against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) have been commercialized recently. In immunocompromised patients, the duration of vaccinal humoral protection as well as the relevance of seasonal revaccination is still unknown. The supplied evidence does not clearly state the core experimental, analytical, or statistical methods. Their immediate immunogenicity in various conditions of immunosuppression, including patients receiving allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), have been reported in 2025 by different teams, including ours. We also provide a first evaluation of vaccinal clinical effectiveness in HSCT patients. By analyzing the kinetics of humoral responses after a single dose of bivalent RSVpreF vaccine over 12 months in 71 HSCT recipients, we show that annual revaccination benefits mostly those primarily vaccinated within the early 18 months after HSCT. This deterministic extraction is based on retrieved fulltext evidence. The source does not explicitly report enough limitations for an independent appraisal, so confidence is low.

title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus–Related Hospitalizations Among Infants Receiving Nirsevimab

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to estimate the effectiveness of nirsevimab in preventing RSV-related hospitalizations among infants, addressing the need to reduce the burden of RSV, a leading cause of hospitalization in this age group.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A test-negative case-control study was conducted in 7 tertiary care pediatric hospitals in Ontario and Quebec, Canada, involving infants tested for RSV between October 27, 2024, and March 1, 2025.
analysis.methods: Infants were stratified by their disposition outcome—ED visit only, hospitalization, or ICU admission—on the day of specimen collection or within the subsequent 14 days. Symptomatic infants younger than 12 months who were tested for RSV were included, with a focus on those who received nirsevimab.
analysis.main_results: Among 1942 eligible encounters, 683 (35.2%) had RSV-positive test results (cases) and 1259 (64.8%) had RSV-negative test results (controls). A lower proportion of cases than controls received nirsevimab (7.0% vs 30.3%; P < .001). The effectiveness of nirsevimab was estimated to be 78% (95% CI, 68%-84%), including 77% against ED visits, 79% against hospitalizations, and 97% against ICU admissions.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that nirsevimab had high estimated effectiveness in preventing RSV disease severity that requires hospital-based care, with consistent results across subgroups and time from receipt.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that nirsevimab has the potential to reduce the burden of RSV, particularly in preventing severe outcomes that require hospitalization.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its design as a test-negative case-control study, which may introduce bias. The high effectiveness of nirsevimab across all subgroups and time from receipt supports the robustness of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of nirsevimab in preventing RSV-related hospitalizations among infants. Among 1942 eligible encounters, nirsevimab was found to be highly effective in preventing severe RSV outcomes, with an estimated effectiveness of 78%.

title: Rapid subtype-specific detection of respiratory syncytial virus A and B using an RNase HII-dependent RT-LAMP lateral flow assay

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to develop a rapid and simultaneous detection method for respiratory syncytial virus A (RSV A) and RSV B with subtype discrimination, important for point-of-care diagnostics and epidemiological surveillance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved developing the RSV A/B rh-RT-LAMP-NALF assay using nasopharyngeal swab specimens from 281 archived clinical samples, including 87 RSV A-positive, 94 RSV B-positive, and 100 RSV-negative specimens, with the AllplexTM Respiratory Panel 1 assay as the reference method.
analysis.methods: The RSV A/B rh-RT-LAMP-NALF assay incorporated blocked inner primers activated by RNase HII to suppress non-specific amplification, and used 5′-FAM– and 5′-DIG–labeled loop primers for RSV A and RSV B detection on a single PCRD multiplex strip.
analysis.main_results: The assay achieved an analytical limit of detection of 4 × 10^1 copies/μL and demonstrated sensitivities of 95.4% (95% CI: 88.8%–98.2%) for RSV A and 97.9% (95% CI: 92.6%–99.4%) for RSV B, with no false-positive results in 100 RSV-negative specimens.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The RSV A/B rh-RT-LAMP-NALF assay provided rapid, accurate, and subtype-specific point-of-care diagnostics for RSV detection and surveillance, comparable to or better than other commercial assays.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The assay can improve the accuracy and speed of RSV detection, aiding in point-of-care diagnostics and epidemiological surveillance, particularly in resource-limited settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of archived specimens and the need for further validation in real-time clinical settings. The evidence strength is moderate due to the use of a single reference method and the absence of randomized controlled trials.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed a rapid and accurate RSV A/B rh-RT-LAMP-NALF assay for simultaneous subtype-specific detection, demonstrating high sensitivity and specificity in clinical specimens. The assay provides a valuable tool for point-of-care diagnostics and surveillance.

title: Genomic characterization of circulating respiratory syncytial virus strains in Lombardy before and after the introduction of nirsevimab prophylaxis

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the impact of nirsevimab prophylaxis on the genomic evolution of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) strains in Lombardy, addressing the need for ongoing monitoring of viral diversification and resistance to inform prevention strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed RSV-positive upper respiratory tract samples collected from patients between October 2023 and March 2025, focusing on sequences from infants and individuals with lower-respiratory-tract infections.
analysis.methods: Whole genomes were obtained using an amplicon protocol, sequenced on Illumina platforms, and assembled with vcf-consensus-builder. Phylogenetic analysis was conducted using maximum-likelihood trees and Bayesian coalescent methods to define clades and large phylogenetic clusters (LPCs).
analysis.main_results: A total of 302 RSV sequences were retrieved, with 72.7% of cases involving lower-respiratory-tract infections, 67.2% requiring hospitalization, and 15.0% admitted to the intensive-care-unit (ICU). Additionally, 17 nirsevimab breakthrough infections (N_BI) were identified, and four large phylogenetic clusters (LPCs) were found, including two new LPCs in the 2024–2025 season.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence of ongoing viral diversification and increased F protein variability, which highlights the importance of genomic surveillance to adapt prophylaxis strategies. This study provides novel insights into the temporal changes in RSV strains in Lombardy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the necessity of continuous genomic surveillance to monitor RSV evolution and resistance, which can inform the development and optimization of prophylaxis strategies, particularly for nirsevimab.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a specific geographic region and time period, and the evidence is based on genomic data without direct clinical outcomes. The confidence in the findings is moderate due to these constraints.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the genomic evolution of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in Lombardy before and after the introduction of nirsevimab prophylaxis. RSV-positive upper respiratory tract samples were collected between October 2023 and March 2025, and whole genomes were sequenced and analyzed using phylogenetic methods. The results showed that 302 RSV sequences were retrieved, with a majority from infants and males, and 72.7% of cases involving lower-respiratory-tract infections. The study identified four large phylogenetic clusters (LPCs), including two new ones in the 2024–2025 season, and found increased variability in the F protein and fewer ICU admissions in the latter period. The authors concluded that ongoing genomic surveillance is essential to monitor RSV diversification and inform prophylaxis strategies. The study's findings are significant for understanding the impact of nirsevimab on viral evolution but are limited by the geographic and temporal scope of the data, resulting in moderate confidence in the conclusions.

title: Structural evolution of ionizable lipids for nucleic acid delivery.

analysis.scope_and_question: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles have emerged as a potent non-viral delivery platform for nucleic acid therapeutics, achieving clinical breakthroughs ranging from the FDA-approved small interfering RNA therapeutic to mRNA vaccines against coronavirus disease 2019 and respiratory syncytial virus.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Over the last several decades, their structures have evolved extensively through the application of combinatorial chemistry, rational design, incorporation of functional elements and, most recently, machine learning and artificial intelligence-guided strategies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: These innovations have expanded ionizable lipids from passive carriers into multifunctional materials capable of organ-specific targeting, responsiveness, immunomodulation and theranostics.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: In this Review, we highlight the development, synthesis and structural evolution of ionizable lipids as well as their emerging on-demand design functionalities and next-generation biomedical applications.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: We provide insights into the challenges and gaps for translation, manufacturing and expansion of lipid nanoparticle-mediated nucleic acid therapeutics for precision RNA medicine.

analysis.summary_en: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles have emerged as a potent non-viral delivery platform for nucleic acid therapeutics, achieving clinical breakthroughs ranging from the FDA-approved small interfering RNA therapeutic to mRNA vaccines against coronavirus disease 2019 and respiratory syncytial virus. Over the last several decades, their structures have evolved extensively through the application of combinatorial chemistry, rational design, incorporation of functional elements and, most recently, machine learning and artificial intelligence-guided strategies. These innovations have expanded ionizable lipids from passive carriers into multifunctional materials capable of organ-specific targeting, responsiveness, immunomodulation and theranostics. In this Review, we highlight the development, synthesis and structural evolution of ionizable lipids as well as their emerging on-demand design functionalities and next-generation biomedical applications. We provide insights into the challenges and gaps for translation, manufacturing and expansion of lipid nanoparticle-mediated nucleic acid therapeutics for precision RNA medicine.

title: Testing the feasibility of a national respiratory swabbing tool in FluSurvey to support pandemic preparedness in England, 2025-26

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on assessing the feasibility of a national respiratory swabbing tool in FluSurvey to support pandemic preparedness in England, specifically targeting respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and its variants. The central question is whether self-swabbing can be effectively implemented among symptomatic participants to detect RSV, Covid-19, and Influenza.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The study was conducted between January and March 2026 in England using FluSurvey, a participatory surveillance system. Participants reporting recent acute respiratory infection symptoms were eligible for self-swabbing PCR tests for RSV, Covid-19, and Influenza. Optional feedback surveys were sent to participants to evaluate their willingness to participate again.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study found that 45.7% of eligible illnesses requested test kits, and 93.5% of these returned them. Of the returned kits, 97.0% provided valid results. The median time from symptom onset to specimen date was 4.0 days. High participant engagement and positive feedback suggest the feasibility of using self-swabbing for respiratory virus surveillance.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report controversies or evidence gaps related to RSV specifically. However, it notes that the study focused on RSV, Covid-19, and Influenza, and the feasibility of self-swabbing for these pathogens was assessed without addressing other respiratory viruses or specific subtypes of RSV.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The tool developed can be rapidly deployed and adapted to public health needs, particularly for assessing community-based emerging respiratory or pandemic infections. The high return rate and positive feedback suggest continued engagement of the cohort in respiratory virus swabbing, which could inform future public health strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the feasibility of a self-swabbing tool for detecting respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), Covid-19, and Influenza within the FluSurvey system in England. The study, conducted between January and March 2026, found that 45.7% of eligible participants requested test kits, with 93.5% returning them. Of these, 97.0% provided valid results, and the median time from symptom onset to specimen collection was 4.0 days. High participant engagement and positive feedback suggest the tool's potential for rapid deployment in public health surveillance. The findings support the use of self-swabbing for community-based respiratory virus monitoring, particularly for emerging infections like RSV.

title: Airway protease availability governs a reversible shift between syncytial and cell-free spread.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate how host protease availability influences the spread of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human parainfluenza virus 3 (HPIV3) in the airway, addressing the gap in understanding whether protease context biases syncytial versus cell-free spread.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study compared RSV and HPIV3 in respiratory cell lines and primary airway cells under defined in vitro protease conditions, focusing on their distinct F cleavage-site compositions and how they interact with the host protease environment.
analysis.methods: The researchers used serine protease inhibitors (SERPINs) to selectively inhibit proteases and observed the effects on viral spread, including syncytium formation and cell-free dissemination, in controlled in vitro settings.
analysis.main_results: In multi-cycle infections, furin-dominant, trypsin-like-low environments produced the largest syncytia, whereas trypsin-like-high environments favored smaller syncytia and more cell-free spread. Exogenous TMPRSS2 addition shifted HPIV3 toward cell-free spread with minimal impact on RSV.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that host protease availability acts as a reversible switch between syncytial and cell-free spread, challenging the traditional view that spread is determined solely by fixed viral features.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results have direct implications for protease-targeting therapeutics, indicating that modulating protease activity could reroute viral spread and potentially reduce tissue damage associated with respiratory infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro conditions, and the evidence is based on abstract-only reporting, which suggests a moderate confidence level in the generalizability of findings to in vivo scenarios.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how host protease availability influences the spread of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human parainfluenza virus 3 (HPIV3) in the airway. It challenges the traditional view that viral spread is determined solely by fixed features of the fusion protein, showing instead that the host protease environment acts as a reversible switch between syncytial and cell-free spread. The study compared these viruses in respiratory cell lines and primary airway cells under defined in vitro protease conditions, revealing that furin-dominant, trypsin-like-low environments promote larger syncytia, while trypsin-like-high environments favor smaller syncytia and more cell-free spread. Exogenous TMPRSS2 addition shifted HPIV3 toward cell-free spread with minimal impact on RSV. The findings suggest that protease-targeting drugs may not simply block infection but redirect how the virus spreads, with potential implications for reducing tissue damage. However, the study is limited to in vitro settings, and the evidence is based on abstract-only reporting, which suggests moderate confidence in the generalizability of results to in vivo scenarios.

title: Post-acute symptom persistence following SARS-CoV-2, RSV, and influenza in children

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the prevalence and patterns of post-acute symptoms following SARS-CoV-2, RSV, and influenza in children, addressing the need to understand the extent and nature of post-acute morbidity beyond SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on children aged 0 to 18 years with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 (n = 1540), RSV (n = 2150), or influenza (n = 2050) infections, evaluated at a tertiary university hospital system in Istanbul, Turkey, from January 2020 to December 2024.
analysis.methods: Persistent symptoms were assessed at follow-up visits 4 to 6 weeks after virological diagnosis using multivariable logistic regression and inverse probability weighting sensitivity analysis. Model calibration and discriminative ability were assessed using the Hosmer-Lemeshow test and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, respectively.
analysis.main_results: Among 5740 children, 24.0% (95% CI = 22.2–25.8) had persistent symptoms after RSV, 22.0% (95% CI = 19.9–24.1) after SARS-CoV-2, and 21.2% (95% CI = 19.4–23.0) after influenza. RSV-related post-acute morbidity was characterized by respiratory and feeding difficulties in young infants, SARS-CoV-2 by neurocognitive and systemic complaints in school-aged children, and influenza by sustained systemic symptoms.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that post-acute symptom persistence following pediatric viral respiratory infections is common and follows virus-specific patterns, extending beyond SARS-CoV-2 and varying by pathogen and age.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the development of pathogen-informed follow-up considerations and highlight the importance of understanding virus-specific post-acute morbidity in children.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and the potential for residual confounding, but the consistent results from inverse probability weighting sensitivity analysis suggest robustness.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated post-acute symptoms in children following SARS-CoV-2, RSV, and influenza infections, finding that while overall post-acute prevalence was comparable across the three viruses, symptom profiles were virus-specific and age-dependent, emphasizing the need for pathogen-informed follow-up care.

title: Respiratory viral infections in patients with inherited metabolic disorders: Pathogen distribution and clinical outcomes.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the epidemiology, viral etiology, and clinical severity of respiratory viral infections in hospitalized children with inherited metabolic disorders (IEMs), addressing the need for better understanding of pathogen-specific outcomes in this population.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A single-center retrospective study was conducted on children with IEMs hospitalized with acute infectious illness and laboratory-confirmed respiratory viral detection during 2018-2024, involving 45 infection episodes among 41 children.
analysis.methods: The study evaluated demographic features, underlying metabolic diagnoses, viral pathogens, and outcomes using retrospective data.
analysis.main_results: A total of 45 infection episodes among 41 children were included; influenza was the most frequently identified virus (35.6%), followed by rhinovirus (22.2%), seasonal coronavirus (sCoV) (13.3%), and respiratory syncytial virus (11.1%). PICU admission was required in 13.3% (6/45) of cases, and infection-related mortality was 6.7% (n = 3), all due to sCoV infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study suggests that respiratory viral infections may be associated with a clinical burden in children with IEMs, highlighting the importance of close clinical monitoring and supportive management in this vulnerable population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that respiratory viral infections, particularly sCoV, may have significant clinical implications in children with IEMs, emphasizing the need for tailored management strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single-center design and the retrospective nature of the data, which may affect generalizability. The sample size is relatively small, and the study does not include specific methods for identifying respiratory syncytial virus, which may introduce bias.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated respiratory viral infections in children with inherited metabolic disorders, finding that influenza was the most common virus, while sCoV was associated with all fatal cases. The findings highlight the clinical burden and the need for close monitoring in this vulnerable population.

title: SARS-CoV-2 Coinfections and Severity in Hospitalized Children With Systematic Testing.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Co-circulation of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) with other respiratory viruses raised concerns that coinfections may increase pediatric coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) severity, but evidence is limited by variable testing practices.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Children aged <17 years hospitalized with confirmed COVID-19 during Delta and Omicron periods were included.
analysis.methods: We analyzed national surveillance data from the Canadian Immunization Monitoring Program, ACTive (IMPACT) COVID-19 study. Coinfection was defined as SARS-CoV-2 plus ≥1 additional respiratory virus. Primary analyses were restricted to centres with systematic multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing of all admissions with acute respiratory illness (n = 5), while secondary analyses included all centres (n = 13). Associations with outcomes (respiratory support, ventilation, intensive care and severe COVID-19) were estimated using multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression and adjusted odds ratios (aORs).
analysis.main_results: Among 2831 hospitalized children, 938 were admitted at centers with systematic multiplex PCR testing, among whom 18.6% had ≥1 respiratory viral coinfection. Respiratory syncytial virus (39.7%) and enterovirus/rhinovirus (38.5%) coinfections were the most common.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In centers that systematically conducted multiplex PCR testing, SARS-CoV-2 respiratory viral coinfections were not associated with increased COVID-19 severity. Differences observed when including centers without systematic testing underscore the importance of considering testing strategies when evaluating the clinical impact of coinfections.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that systematic testing strategies may be critical for accurately assessing the clinical impact of SARS-CoV-2 coinfections in hospitalized children, which has implications for improving surveillance and understanding disease severity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the reliance on surveillance data and the potential for variability in testing practices across centers, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between SARS-CoV-2 coinfections and severity in hospitalized children, focusing on the impact of systematic testing strategies. It found that in centers with consistent multiplex PCR testing, coinfections were not linked to increased severity, but when including all centers, coinfections were associated with higher odds of severe outcomes. The results highlight the importance of standardized testing in evaluating the clinical significance of coinfections. The study's reliance on surveillance data and variability in testing practices limits the strength of the evidence, suggesting a moderate confidence level in its conclusions.
